profiles.name: the AVD that produced the mislabelled sessions
profiles.note: ro.* from a booted API 34 AVD. An archive on this machine holds 18 sessions from this exact image recorded as android-device, which is the defect the Kotlin rule exists for.

profiles.name: the newest AVD image
profiles.note: ro.* from a booted API 37 AVD. Different device and product strings from the API 34 image, which is the churn the old marketing-string match could not survive.

profiles.name: the strings the old check looked for
profiles.note: An older AVD, the shape the replaced check was written against. Keeping it passing is the whole reason the marketing-string rules were kept rather than deleted.

profiles.name: hardware alone is enough
profiles.note: Every other field blank, so this asserts the ro.hardware rule and nothing else. It is the rule that is meant to hold when image branding changes again.

profiles.name: the product alone is enough
profiles.note: Every field blank but the product, which JS reads out of the fingerprint. On every real image here the device or the model fires as well, so without this nothing would show that the product is read at all; it does for the product what 'hardware alone is enough' does for the hardware.

profiles.name: Cuttlefish
profiles.note: Cuttlefish, Android's own cloud emulator. Its brand and fingerprint carry no emulator tell, so in JS the device and product taken from the fingerprint are what fire.

profiles.name: a Pixel
profiles.note: Representative vendor values, not transcribed from attached hardware: no phone has been attached. ro.hardware is the SoC codename, never a QEMU board.

profiles.name: a Samsung
profiles.note: Representative vendor values, not transcribed from attached hardware. ro.hardware is the vendor platform.

profiles.name: nothing known
profiles.note: A JVM unit test against the stock android.jar sees null for every Build field. The answer there is uninformative either way; what matters is that it is an answer.
